titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spells 74, 8, 2, 9, 132 and 10
part: Spells 74, 8, 2, 9, 132 and 10 — walking, going forth by day, living after death and returning home (Plate 18)
about: Six short spells written one after another on Plate 18 of Ani's papyrus, after Spells 43, 89, 91 and 92. Spell 74 gives the dead man the use of his legs; Spells 8, 2 and 9 open the West and the world below to him so that he may go forth by day and live after death, as the Moon, as the son of Osiris and as a glorious spirit; Spell 132 lets him come back to see his house on earth; and Spell 10 (Budge's Chapter XLVIII) sends him out against his enemies. Many words are rare and several signs in Budge's print are uncertain; the notes say where a reading is doubtful, and the last spell breaks off in mid-thought.

sentences.l: spell · of · hastening(?) · the-legs · going-forth · upon · earth
sentences.i: Spell for hastening(?) the legs and going forth upon earth.
sentences.n: Spell 74 begins, written in red. rꜣ n 'spell of' is the mouth with its stroke and water n, as in every title. wnt is the hare wn with water n as complement, t and the walking legs as classifier: wn 'hasten, hurry', the verb of motion written with the legs (as in Spells 46 and 92), here its infinitive with t; Budge has 'walking', and the sense is doubtful. rdwy 'the two legs' is the leg with its foot (D56) printed twice, the first as the word-sign rd, the second for the dual; the ending wy is not written. No preposition stands between them: 'hastening the legs', making them move quickly. pr 'going forth' is the house pr with r and the walking legs, the infinitive of pri. tꜣ 'earth' is the strip of land with grains (coded N16, approximate). The dead man asks for the use of his legs, so that he can walk out of the tomb.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · may-do-you · deeds-your · for(?) · Sokar · (twice)
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: Do what you do (for me?), Sokar (Twice.),
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i and r; read in. ḏd in N 'said by N' is written in red: the cobra with an upright stroke under its neck, the cobra-and-hand ligature of this type, coded I10 and D46 (the hand approximate), then the reed over a lens-shaped sign that is the mouth r, where water n belongs; the formula allows only in. wsir is the low seat (coded Q2, approximate) over the eye, in black. ir·k is the eye ir with r as complement and the basket ·k: the sḏm·f of iri 'do', here a wish or command, 'may you do'. irt·k is the same eye and r with t, plural strokes and ·k: the noun irt 'what is done, deeds', from iri (not irt 'eye'), 'your deeds'. Water n follows and is not clear: perhaps the preposition 'for' with its object 'me' not written, or the genitive 'your deeds of (= as) Sokar'; the translation marks it doubtful. skr 'Sokar' is the bolt s, the basket k and r with the seated god (Budge: Seker). sp sn '(Twice.)' is the threshing floor sp (O50) and two upright strokes: the call is to be said twice. Sokar is the falcon god of the Memphite cemetery, made one with Osiris; his feast was the moving of his bark, and he is asked here to do his work in the dead man.

sentences.l: who-is-in · cavern-his · who-is-in(?) · legs-my · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: who is in his cavern, who is in(?) my legs in the necropolis.
sentences.n: imy 'who is in' is the crossed planks im with the owl m as complement and two strokes y: the nisba of m 'in', here after the name it describes. qrrt·f 'his cavern' is the hill-slope q, the mouth r twice and t, with a small open circle (coded N33, approximate) as classifier and ·f (Budge: qerert, 'dwelling-place'); a larger cavern sign is not printed. The second imy is written the same way. rdwy·i 'my legs' is the leg (D56) twice and the seated man ·i, the dual ending not written. imy rdwy·i is taken with Sokar, 'who is in my legs', as if the god's power were to move them; the sense is doubtful. ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis' is the flag nṯr written first out of respect, a small loop for r (coded D21, approximate) and the block ẖr (T28) (Budge: Neter-χert). Sokar's cavern is his shrine in the world below.

sentences.l: I · one-who-shines · who-is-over · the-Leg · of-the-sky
sentences.i: I am one who shines, who is over the Leg of the Sky.
sentences.n: ink 'I' is the pot in (W24) with k and the seated man as classifier: ink with a noun, 'I am …'. psd 'one who shines' is p, the bolt s and a low flat hand d, with the sun shedding rays (N8) as classifier: the participle of psḏ 'shine', spelled with the hand d for ḏ, as in the Hymn to Ra. ḥry 'who is over' is the face ḥr with r, two strokes y and the sky as classifier: the nisba of ḥr 'upon'. wꜥrt 'the Leg' is a single leg with its foot (D56), the word-sign, with t as complement (Budge: uārt); wꜥrt pt, 'the Leg of the Sky', is a direct genitive, and pt 'sky' is p and t with the sky sign. The Leg is taken as a region of the sky; what place is meant is not clear.

sentences.l: come-forth-I · from · the-sky · sit(?)-I · at · the-Spirit
sentences.i: I come forth from the sky and sit(?) beside the Spirit.
sentences.n: pr·i 'I come forth' is the house pr with r, the walking legs and the seated man ·i: the sḏm·f of pri. m pt 'from the sky' as before. ḥfd·i is the wick ḥ, the viper f and the hand d, with a man seated as if on a chair with one arm raised (coded A50, approximate) as classifier and ·i (Budge: ḥefṭ-à): a verb ḥfd, taken by its classifier as 'sit, settle'; the sense is doubtful. ḥr 'at, beside' is the face with its stroke. ꜣḫw is the crested ibis ꜣḫ (G25) and the chick w, with the sun with rays and the seated god as classifiers (Budge's numeral 3 is printed inside the word): ꜣḫ 'spirit', here a god who shines, perhaps the sun himself. The dead man rises to the sky and takes his seat among the gods of light.

sentences.l: O · weary-am-I · (twice) · walk-I · weary-am-I
sentences.i: O, I am weary (Twice.)! I walk, and I am weary
sentences.n: i 'O' is the reed with a standing man raising one arm (coded A26, approximate): a cry. nn·kwi 'I am weary' is two rush plants and two water lines, n twice with its complements, then the weary man sitting with arms hanging (coded A7, approximate) and a small bird of bad things (G37) as classifiers, and the basket k with the seated man for the stative ending ·kwi 'I', its w not written: the stative of nni 'be weary, inert', the state of the dead before they are raised (Budge: enen-kuà). sp sn '(Twice.)'. šmt·i 'I walk' is the pool š (coded N37, approximate) on walking legs, the owl m, t, the legs again and ·i, written as in Spell 147: šm 'go, walk', with t. nn·kwi is said again.

sentences.l: in · the-face · of-the-teeth(?) · that-seize(?) · [mouth]-their · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: before the teeth(?) that seize(?) — [their mouth] — in the necropolis.
sentences.n: m ḥr 'in the face of, before' is the owl m and the face with its stroke and r (Budge's numeral 4 is printed before the r). ibḥw 'the teeth' is a small tusk (coded F18, approximate), the sign of the tooth, over plural strokes (Budge: ābeḥ); the reed i is not printed. ṯꜣ is a duckling with raised wings (coded G47, approximate), the sign ṯꜣ, with the vulture ꜣ as complement: taken as ṯꜣ 'seize, snatch', a participle 'that seize' (Budge: 'gnasheth'). Budge prints rꜣ 'mouth' (the mouth and its stroke) in square brackets as restored, and ·sn 'their' (the bolt, water n and plural strokes) as a separate group; they are joined here as rꜣ·sn (q re-indexed). The words do not join into a clear sentence: the teeth and the mouths are perhaps those of the beings of the world below who devour the dead, before whom the weary man has to walk. m ẖrt-nṯr 'in the necropolis' is written in full: the flag, the block ẖr over r, t over the hills.

sentences.l: the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · in · peace
sentences.i: The Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice, in peace.
sentences.n: wsir is written here with the eye, the tall seat and the seated god. sš 'scribe' is the scribe's palette with its water pot and pen (Y3; Budge reads it ān, an old value). ꜣny has a squatting man holding a flail (A52) as classifier. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' is written short, the plinth mꜣꜥ over the oar ḫrw, without the sickle. m ḥtp 'in peace' is the bar m and the offering mat ḥtp (R4) with t and p as complements and the papyrus roll. Spell 74 ends with Ani's name and the wish that he rest in peace.

sentences.l: [spell · of] · traversing(?) · the-West · [going-forth] · by · day
sentences.i: [Spell for] traversing(?) the West and [going forth] by day.
sentences.n: Spell 8 begins; Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The title is written in red. Budge prints rꜣ n 'spell of' and the group prt 'going forth' in square brackets: they are his restorations of damaged places, kept here. ꜥbꜣ is an upright staff with a small ring at its top and foot (coded S42, approximate), the sceptre ꜥbꜣ, then the foot b, the jabiru bꜣ (G29) as complements and a tall upright with a tie (coded Y1a, approximate) as classifier (Budge: āba, 'passing through'). The signs give ꜥbꜣ; a verb of that spelling meaning 'pass through' is not otherwise known to this edition, and the sense rests on Budge and on the title of Spell 9, where the same word stands before the Imhet. imntt 'the West' is the emblem of the West with t twice and the hills. prt m hrw 'going forth by day': prt is the house, r, t and the legs; hrw is the sun with its stroke. The West is the land of the dead, which the dead man must cross before he can come out into the day.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · is-opened · Wenu · is-sealed · the-head(?) · of-Thoth
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: Wenu is opened, and the head(?) of Thoth is sealed.
sentences.n: ḏd in is written in red (the cobra-and-hand ligature, the hand coded D46, approximate; in is the reed over water n); wsir, with the low seat (coded Q2, approximate) over the eye, is black. wn·w is the hare wn with n, the chick w and the low hooked sign (U15) as classifier: the passive sḏm of wn 'open', with the w that this form sometimes writes, 'is opened' (Budge: unu). wnw is the hare, n, the pot nw and the chick, with the town sign (O49): Wenu, the city of Thoth (Budge: Unnu; the Greeks called it Hermopolis). ḫtm 'is sealed' is ḫ, t, the owl m and a seal on its necklace (S20) as classifier, the passive again. Budge's numeral 2 stands before tp, the head (coded D1, approximate: the type shows a rounded blob), followed by the kneeling man as classifier. After tp Budge prints four dots in his transliteration, but no gap in the signs; the seated man, which does not usually follow tp, may be what he could not read, and the sense 'head' is doubtful. ḏḥwty 'Thoth' is the ibis on its standard with t and two strokes y. Wenu, Thoth's city, is where the world was said to begin; the opening and sealing are perhaps of his shrine.

sentences.l: excellent · is-the-Eye · of-Horus · which-binds(?) · me · the-Eye · of-Horus · glorious · (is)-ornaments-my · on · the-brow · of-Ra · the-father · of-the-gods
sentences.i: Excellent is the Eye of Horus, which binds(?) me; the glorious Eye of Horus is my ornament on the brow of Ra, the father of the gods.
sentences.n: iqr 'excellent' is the reed, the hill-slope q, r and a flat roll (Y1) as classifier: an adjective put first as the predicate, 'excellent is …'. irt ḥr 'the Eye of Horus' is the plain eye with t and its stroke, and the falcon with a stroke. Budge prints seśeṭu-à as one group; it is split here into sšd and wi (q re-indexed), as in the same words in Spell 92: sšd is a looped cord (coded V6, approximate) for sš and the low flat hand d, a participle after its noun, 'which binds(?)' (Budge: 'I have delivered'), the sense doubtful; wi 'me' is the chick w and the kneeling man, the dependent pronoun. irt ḥr again, the falcon alone. ꜣḫ 'glorious' is the crested ibis, ḫ and the roll: an adjective after its noun. ḫkrw is the belly of an animal (coded F32, approximate) written for ḫ, the basket k and r, an ornament of the frieze ḫkr (coded Aa30, approximate), the roll and a stroke (Budge: χakeru, 'splendours'). After it stands the kneeling man alone, under which Budge prints only dots; it is taken here as the suffix ·i 'my', as in Spell 92 (ḫkrw·i, with a stroke and the seated man), and joined to the word (q re-indexed). The sentence has no verb: 'the glorious Eye of Horus (is) my ornaments'. m wpt rꜥ 'on the brow of Ra': the bar m, the horns wp (coded F13, approximate) with t and a stroke, and rꜥ with r, a flat arm ꜥ (coded D36, approximate) and the seated god with the sun disc. Budge's numeral 3 stands before itf 'father', the reed, t and the viper f with a seated figure (coded A1, approximate: the type shows a long-wigged figure). nṯrw 'the gods' is the flag three times. The Eye of Horus is the uraeus on the sun's brow; the dead man wears it as his own crown.

sentences.l: [I] · Osiris · that · this(?) · [who-is-in] · the-West
sentences.i: [I am] that Osiris(?) [who is in] the West.
sentences.n: Budge's numeral 3 stands before this line. ink 'I' (the pot and the basket) is in Budge's square brackets, restored. wsir is the low seat (coded Q2, approximate) over the eye. pwy 'that' is p, the chick w and two reeds y: the demonstrative after its noun. nn is two rush plants and two water lines, written as nn 'these, this' (Budge: enen, 'same'); after pwy it is not clear, and is taken as a second demonstrative, 'that one, this one'. imy 'who is in' (the crossed planks and the owl, the y not written) is restored in Budge's brackets. imntt 'the West' is the emblem of the West, t twice and the hills. The dead man claims to be Osiris himself, the lord of the West.

sentences.l: has-learned · Osiris · day-his · not-does-he · exist · there · not · exist-I · there
sentences.i: Osiris knows his day on which(?) he does not exist there; I do not exist there.
sentences.n: Budge prints reχ and en as two groups; they are joined here as rḫ·n (q re-indexed): the mouth r, the placenta ḫ and the roll, with water n, the sḏm·n·f of rḫ, 'has learned', that is, 'knows'. wsir with the low seat (coded Q2, approximate). hrw·f 'his day' is the house plan h (O4), r, the chick w and the sun, and ·f; Budge prints O4 in one pair of square brackets and the chick and the sun in another, as restored. tm·f wnn im: tm is t, the sledge tm (U15) and the owl m with the roll, and ·f, the negative verb 'not to do', with wnn 'exist, be' (the hare, n and n) as the verb it negates, 'he does not exist'; im 'there' is the reed and the owl. It is taken as a clause describing hrw·f, 'his day (on which) he is not there'. n wnn·i im: the negative arms (coded D35, approximate) and wnn·i 'I exist', 'I do not exist there'; Budge's numeral 4 stands before the second im. The sense is not clear: the dead man seems to share the fate of Osiris, absent from the place where the god is absent.

sentences.l: I · the-Moon · who-is-among · the-gods · not · shall-come-to-an-end-I
sentences.i: I am the Moon among the gods; I shall not come to an end.
sentences.n: ink 'I am'. iꜥḥ 'the Moon' is written with one sign only, a seated god with the crescent and disc on his head (coded A40, approximate): the moon god as a word-sign (Budge: àāḥ). imy nṯrw 'who is among the gods': imy as before, nṯrw the flag three times. nn tm·i: the negative arms (coded D35, approximate) and water n, nn with the sḏm·f, the negative of the future; tm·i is the sledge tm with t and m and ·i, here tm 'be complete, come to an end' (not the negative verb). The moon wanes and comes back: like it, the dead man is never finished.

sentences.l: stand-up · then-you · Horus · counts-he · you · among · the-gods
sentences.i: Stand up, then, Horus! He counts you among the gods.
sentences.n: ꜥḥꜥ 'stand up' is the mast ꜥḥꜥ (P6) with a flat arm ꜥ (coded D36, approximate) as complement and the walking legs: the imperative. ir·k is the reed, the mouth r and ·k: the word r with a suffix that follows a command to strengthen it, 'you, then'. ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon, here called on. Budge prints àp-f-tu as one group; it is split here into ip·f and tw (q re-indexed). ip·f is the reed, p and a flat roll (Y1) as classifier, and ·f: the sḏm·f of ip 'count, reckon', 'he counts', whose subject is not named. tw 'you' is t and the chick w, the dependent pronoun, as object. m-m 'among' is the owl m and a second owl joined to the arm ꜥ in one ligature; the arm, from the later spelling with ꜥ, is not read. nṯrw 'the gods' is the flag with a short stroke before it and a dashed stroke after it as plural strokes. Spell 8 ends here: Horus, the son, is counted among the gods, as the dead man hopes to be.

sentences.l: spell · of · going-forth · by · day · and-living · after · death
sentences.i: Spell for going forth by day and living after death.
sentences.n: Spell 2 begins, written in red. prt m hrw 'going forth by day': prt is the house, r, t and the walking legs (the t printed beside the r); hrw is the house plan h, r, the sun and a stroke. ꜥnḫ 'living' is the sign of life ꜥnḫ with n and ḫ as complements, the infinitive, joined to prt without 'and'. m-ḫt 'after' is the owl m, the placenta ḫ, a branch ḫt (M3) and t, with the walking legs. mt 'death' is a flat sign with an upright tab at its right end, coded U15 for what is printed, standing where the bar m is expected (Budge reads mit), then t and a small open circle (coded N33, approximate) as classifier: mwt 'die', here the infinitive 'dying, death', written without w. To live after death is what all the spells of going forth by day promise.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · O · One · who-rises · as · the-Moon
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: O One who rises as the Moon!
sentences.n: ḏd in is in red; wsir (the low seat, coded Q2, approximate, over the eye) is black. Ani's classifier, the kneeling man, is in Budge's square brackets, restored. i 'O' is the reed with a standing man raising an arm (coded A26, approximate). wꜥ 'One' is the harpoon wꜥ (T21) with a stroke and a low flat sign with an upright tab (coded U15 for what is printed) standing for the arm ꜥ as complement (Budge reads ā): 'the One, the Unique'. wbn 'who rises' is the chick w and the foot b, with a disc with hanging rays (coded N8, approximate) as classifier; its n is not written: the participle of wbn 'rise, shine forth'. m 'as' (Budge: 'from'). iꜥḥ 'the Moon' is the seated moon god with crescent and disc (coded A40, approximate), written alone. The One who rises as the Moon is the god who shines in the night sky, perhaps Thoth or Osiris.

sentences.l: O · One · who-shines · as · the-Moon
sentences.i: O One who shines as the Moon!
sentences.n: The call is repeated with another verb. i (A26, approximate) and wꜥ as before. psd 'who shines' is p, the bolt s and below it an elongated sign in the place of the hand d (coded D46, approximate), with a sign of slanting rays (coded N8, approximate) and the sun as classifiers: the participle of psḏ 'shine', with d for ḏ, as in Spell 74. m iꜥḥ 'as the Moon', the moon god again (coded A40, approximate).

sentences.l: let-come-forth · the-Osiris · Ani · this · among · multitude-your · that · (which-is)-outside
sentences.i: Let this Osiris Ani come forth among that multitude of yours which is outside.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the eye ir at the head of rwty; read rwty. prt is written as in the title, house, r, t and the walking legs: with the noun after it, it is taken as a wish, 'let (him) come forth', the t not explained. wsir with the low seat (coded Q2, approximate); ꜣny with the kneeling man; pn 'this' is p and n. m 'among' is the bar m (Aa15). ꜥšꜣt·k 'your multitude' is the lizard ꜥšꜣ (I1) over plural strokes, t and ·k. twy 'that' is t, the chick w and two reeds y, the feminine demonstrative agreeing with ꜥšꜣt. The last word is the eye ir and r, the chick w, t, two strokes y and a house sign (O1), with Budge's numeral 3 printed after the eye and r; Budge's footnote (left out) corrects the eye to a second mouth r, which gives rwty 'outside, the outer (place)', the nisba of rwt 'gate, outside', with the house as classifier. 'Those outside' are the living, or the gods of the open sky, among whom the dead man would walk.

sentences.l: establish(?) · him · being-in(?) · among · the-spirits · is-opened · to-him · the-Duat
sentences.i: Establish(?) him among the spirits; the Duat is opened to him.
sentences.n: The first word is doubtful. Its first sign is a hatched, domed shape with crossed lines like a tail at its left, lying on a base line, which has no good code and is coded K1 (a fish) although the shape is not that sign; then a low flat sign with an upright tab (U15), the coil w (Z7) and the same flat sign with its left end curled up (U15). Budge reads uāu, 'let be established'. It is read here wꜥw by Budge's letters, the first U15 standing for the arm ꜥ as in wꜥ above and the second as classifier; no word wꜥw of that sense is known to this edition, and both reading and sense are guesses. sw 'him' is the sedge sw (M23) with the chick w: the dependent pronoun, the object. imyw is the crossed planks im, the coil w and two strokes: the plural nisba 'who are in', which here doubles the m that follows, 'among'. ꜣḫw 'the spirits' is written with the sun with hanging rays (coded N8, approximate) as a word-sign for ꜣḫ, the chick w, and a seated figure (coded A40, approximate) as classifier (Budge: χu, 'shining ones'): the dead who have become shining spirits. Budge prints unu-nef as one group; it is split here into wn·w and n·f (q re-indexed). wn·w is the hare, n, the chick w and a hatched door-bolt (O31) over the low hooked sign (U15) as classifiers: the passive 'is opened', as in Spell 8. n·f 'to him' is water n and ·f. dwꜣt 'the Duat' is the star, the vulture ꜣ, t and an open-bottomed house sign (Budge: Ṭuat). The Duat, the world below through which the sun passes by night, is opened before him.

sentences.l: now · the-Osiris · (Osiris) · Ani · (is)-going-forth · by · day · to · do · will-his · upon · earth · among · the-living
sentences.i: Now the Osiris Ani is going forth by day, to do what he wishes upon earth among the living.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes wsir twice; read it once. isk 'now' is the reed, a folded cloth s (S29) and the basket k: the particle that opens a statement. wsir is written first with the low seat (coded Q2, approximate) over the eye, then again, after Budge's numeral 4, with the eye, the tall seat and the seated god; Budge prints '(sic)' after the second. ꜣny with the kneeling man. prt is the house, r, t and the legs: the infinitive after its subject, with the preposition ḥr of 'is doing' not written, 'is going forth'. m hrw 'by day', hrw with the house plan h, r and the sun. r irt 'to do' is r with the infinitive of iri, the eye and t. mrt·f 'his will, what he wishes' is the hoe mr (U6) with r and t, the man with hand to mouth (A2) as classifier, and ·f: the relative form of mri 'love, wish'. tp tꜣ 'upon earth': tp is the head with its stroke, tꜣ the strip of land (coded N16, approximate). m-m 'among' is the owl twice, the second joined to the flat arm. ꜥnḫw 'the living' is ꜥnḫ with n and ḫ, the chick w, the kneeling man and a thin dashed stroke. Spell 2 ends here: the dead man goes out to live among the living.

sentences.l: spell · (of) · going-forth · by · day · after · traversing(?) · the-Imhet
sentences.i: Spell for going forth by day after traversing(?) the Imhet.
sentences.n: Spell 9 begins; the title is written in red. rꜣ is the mouth and its stroke, with no n after it. prt is the house, r and t, without the walking legs. hrw is the sun and its stroke. m-ḫt 'after' as in Spell 2. ꜥbꜣ is the sceptre (coded S42, approximate: an upright with a ring on top, a block, a pendant strand and a crossed ring at its foot), the foot b, the jabiru bꜣ, the vulture ꜣ and a tall upright with a tie as classifier: the word of the title of Spell 8, taken as 'traversing' (Budge: āba, 'having traversed'), its sense doubtful. imḥt is the reed, an owl m drawn without head or ears (coded G17, approximate), the bar m, the wick ḥ, t and an open-bottomed house sign (Budge: àmmeḥet, 'the tomb'): the Imhet, a region of the world below, a cavern or tomb-shaft through which the dead pass. The title promises that the dead man will come out into the day once he has passed through it.

sentences.l: said · by · Ani · O · Ba · great · of-awe
sentences.i: Said by Ani: O Ba, great of awe!
sentences.n: ḏd in is in red. No wsir is written before ꜣny, and Ani's name has no classifier; Budge's '[Osiris]' is in his English only. i 'O' is the reed and a standing man raising an arm (coded A26, approximate). bꜣ 'Ba' is the jabiru bꜣ with the small bowl (R7) printed at its foot and not read, and a small stroke. ꜥꜣ 'great' is the lozenge-tipped column (coded O29, approximate) and a flat roll (Y1). šfyt 'awe, dignity' is a ram's head (F7), the word-sign, standing on a flat bar coded as the pool š (N37, approximate) and t: ꜥꜣ šfyt, 'great of awe', an adjective with a noun after it. The great Ba is a god, perhaps the ba of Osiris, to whom the dead man comes.

sentences.l: see · me · have-come-I · see-I · you · traverse(?)-I · the-Duat · see-I · father-his(?) · Osiris
sentences.i: See, I have come; I see you, I traverse(?) the Duat, I see his(?) father Osiris.
sentences.n: mk is the owl m joined to the arm ꜥ (not read) and the basket k: the particle 'see, behold'. After it the kneeling man stands alone for wi 'me', the dependent pronoun, here written without its w; Budge's māk-à is one group, kept as one word mk-wi. ii·kwi 'I have come' is the reed with legs (M18) ii, the reed and two strokes as complements, the walking legs, and the stative ending ·kwi, k, w and the seated man. Budge prints maa-à-tu as one group; it is split here into mꜣꜣ·i and tw (q re-indexed): mꜣꜣ·i is the eye with the sickle mꜣ over it, two vultures and ·i, the sḏm·f 'I see'; tw 'you' is t and the chick, the dependent pronoun. ꜥbꜣ·i is the sceptre (coded S42, approximate), b, the jabiru and the roll, with ·i: the verb of the title, 'I traverse(?)'. dwꜣt 'the Duat'. mꜣꜣ·i again, with a thin dashed stroke after it before Budge's numeral 3. itf·f is the reed, t and f, then a second viper and a seated figure: 'his father' as it stands (Budge: àtef-f, '[my] father'). The ·f has no one to refer to, and 'my father' is likely, as in the next lines, but both readings are possible and the papyrus is translated as it stands. wsir with the low seat (coded Q2, approximate).

sentences.l: drive-away-I · the-darkness · I · beloved-his
sentences.i: I drive away the darkness; I am his beloved.
sentences.n: sḥr·i is the bolt s, a small face ḥr (coded D2, approximate) with r and two strokes, and a sign like a road with shrubs (coded N31, approximate) as classifier, then ·i: sḥr 'drive away, remove', the sḏm·f, 'I drive away' (Budge: seḥeri-à). kkw 'the darkness' is the basket k twice, two strokes, the chick w and the sky with a star hanging from it (coded N2, approximate), the sign of night. ink 'I am'. mry·f 'his beloved' is the hoe mr with r, two reeds y and the man with hand to mouth (A2), with ·f: the passive participle of mri 'love', 'the one he loves', referring to the father Osiris.

sentences.l: have-come-I · (that)-may-see-I · father-my · Osiris
sentences.i: I have come that I may see my father Osiris.
sentences.n: ii·n·i 'I have come' is the reed with legs, the reed and two strokes, the walking legs, water n and ·i: the sḏm·n·f of ii. mꜣꜣ·i 'that I may see' is the eye with the sickle, two vultures and ·i: the sḏm·f after a verb of motion, expressing purpose. Budge's numeral 4 stands before itf·i 'my father': the reed, t and f, then a second viper, which is not read (Budge prints dots for it), a seated figure as classifier, and a second seated figure, the suffix ·i, which Budge prints in square brackets as restored. wsir with the low seat (coded Q2, approximate).

sentences.l: have-cut-out-I · the-heart · this · of · Seth · who-did · things · against · father-my · Osiris
sentences.i: I have cut out this heart of Seth, who did things against my father Osiris.
sentences.n: ḥsq·i is the wick ḥ, the folded cloth s, the hill-slope q printed as a small triangle (coded N29, approximate) above a slanting knife (coded T30, approximate) as classifier, and ·i: ḥsq 'cut off, cut out', the sḏm·f, here of a deed done (Budge: ḥesq-à). ib pn 'this heart' is the heart jar (F34) with its stroke and pn. n 'of' is water n. swty 'Seth' is the sedge sw, the chick w, t and two strokes y with the seated god (Budge: Suti): a writing of the name of Seth, as in Spell 17. ir 'who did' is the eye and r: the participle of iri. ḫt 'things' is ḫ and t with a flat roll and plural strokes: 'things done', here evil deeds. r 'against'. itf·i 'my father' is the reed, t and f, a seated figure as classifier and a second seated figure ·i. wsir (Q2, approximate). Seth murdered Osiris; the son who avenges his father cuts out the murderer's heart.

sentences.l: have-opened-I · way · every · which-is-in · the-sky · which-is-in · the-earth
sentences.i: I have opened every way that is in the sky and on earth.
sentences.n: Budge's numeral 5 stands before wn·n·i, the hare wn with n, a hatched door-bolt (O31) over the low hooked sign (U15) as classifiers, water n and ·i: the sḏm·n·f of wn 'open', 'I have opened' (Budge: un-nà). wꜣt 'way' is the road with shrubs (coded N31, approximate) with t and a stroke. nb 'every' is the basket alone; the t of the feminine, to agree with wꜣt, is not written. imy is written twice with the reed and the crossed planks im: the nisba 'which is in', its y and the t of the feminine not written. pt 'the sky'; tꜣ 'the earth' is the strip of land (coded N16, approximate). The son who has avenged his father may go where he will, above and below.

sentences.l: I · the-son · who-loves · father-his · Osiris
sentences.i: I am the son who loves his father Osiris.
sentences.n: ink 'I am'. sꜣ 'son' is the pintail duck sꜣ (G39) alone. mry 'who loves' is the hoe mr with r, two reeds y and the man with hand to mouth: the active participle of mri. itf·f 'his father' is the reed, t, f and the viper ·f, followed by three seated figures, all taken as classifiers; why three are printed is not clear. wsir is the eye, the tall seat and the seated god. sꜣ mry it·f, 'the son who loves his father', is the title of the priest who buries and serves his father, as Horus did for Osiris.

sentences.l: am-ennobled-I · am-glorious-I · am-equipped-I
sentences.i: I am ennobled, I am glorious, I am equipped.
sentences.n: Budge's numeral 6 stands before these three statives, each with the ending ·kwi 'I' written k, the chick w and a stroke for i. sꜥḥ·kwi is the bolt s, a low flat sign with an upright tab (coded U15) standing for the arm ꜥ, the wick ḥ, a loop crossed by a band (coded V38, approximate) and a tall upright with a tie (Y1a) as classifiers: the verb sꜥḥ 'be ennobled, have the dignity of a noble' (Budge: sāḥ-kuà), from the noun sꜥḥ 'noble, the noble body of the dead'. ꜣḫ·kwi is the crested ibis ꜣḫ (coded G25, approximate), ḫ, the chick w and the upright with a tie: 'I am glorious, an effective spirit'. ꜥpr·kwi is the bag ꜥpr (Aa20) with r and a flat roll (Y1): 'I am equipped'; its chick w and stroke are in Budge's square brackets, restored. These are the three conditions of the blessed dead: dignity, power, and the equipment of spells.

sentences.l: O · god · every · spirit · every · make · for-me · a-way · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice
sentences.i: O every god and every spirit, make a way for me, the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice!
sentences.n: i 'O' is the reed with the standing man raising an arm (coded A26, approximate). nṯr nb 'every god' is the flag with the seated god and the basket. ꜣḫ nb 'every spirit' is the crested ibis (coded G25, approximate) with a stroke and a seated figure (coded A40, approximate) as classifiers. Budge prints àri-nà as one group; it is split here into ir and n·i (q re-indexed): ir is the eye alone, the imperative of iri 'make'; n·i 'for me' is water n and the seated man. wꜣt 'a way' is the road with shrubs (coded N31, approximate) with t and a stroke. wsir sš ꜣny mꜣꜥ-ḫrw stands after n·i as the speaker's name: the eye, the tall seat and the god; the scribe's palette; ꜣny with the kneeling man; the plinth over the oar, without the sickle. Spell 9 ends here.

sentences.l: spell · of · letting · turn-back · himself · a-man · to · see · house-his · upon · earth
sentences.i: Spell for letting a man turn back to see his house upon earth.
sentences.n: Spell 132 begins; the title is written in red under the long rule that opens the chapter. rdit 'letting' is the mouth r, t and a flat arm (D36, no loaf), the t printed between them. rr is a long rounded loop lying flat (coded V10, approximate), the sign of going round, over the walking legs, without the second r of the writing in Spell 147: rr 'go round, turn about', the sḏm·f after rdit (Budge: rer, 'to return'). sw is the sedge sw with the chick w: the dependent pronoun, here the object, 'himself'. s 'a man' is the bolt s, a stroke and the seated man: the subject, which follows its pronoun object as the rule requires, 'that a man turn himself back'. r mꜣꜣ 'to see' is r with the infinitive, the eye with the sickle joined to it and two vultures. pr·f 'his house' is the house plan with its stroke and ·f. tp tꜣ 'upon earth': the head and stroke, and the strip of land (coded N16, approximate). The dead man is to come back and visit the house he lived in.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · this · I · the-Lion · who-comes-forth · with · striding(?)
sentences.i: Said by this Osiris Ani: I am the Lion, who comes forth with long strides(?).
sentences.n: ḏd in is in red, under a short line that ends before wsir: the cobra-and-hand ligature, and the reed over water n. wsir has the low seat (coded Q2, approximate) over the eye; ꜣny has no classifier; pn 'this' is p and n. ink 'I am'. The next group is a recumbent lion (E23), the sign rw, over a stroke, with the seated god as classifier; Budge prints only dots for it in his transliteration and 'the Lion-god' in his English. It is read rw 'lion', the lion as a god. Budge's numeral 2 stands before pr 'who comes forth', the house, r and the walking legs: the participle of pri. m 'with'. pḏ is p over a long low sign taken as the bow pḏ (coded T9, approximate), and a bar with down-turned ends (coded N1, approximate) over the walking legs as classifiers: pḏ 'stretch', of the stride, as in pḏ nmtt 'stretch the strides' in Spell 92, here the infinitive, 'striding' (Budge: peṭ, 'strides'). The bow sign may hint at the shooting that follows. The lion is a form of the sun god, and the dead man comes out with his power.

sentences.l: (iw) · have-shot-I · (iw) · have-wounded(?)-I · (twice)
sentences.i: I have shot, I have wounded(?) (Twice.)
sentences.n: iw is the reed and the chick w, opening each statement; it is printed twice. sti·n·i is an arrow (T11) over t twice, the low hooked sign (U15) as classifier, water n and ·i (Budge: satet-nà, 'shot arrows'): the sḏm·n·f of sti 'shoot', the arrow standing for st and the two t as complements; the arrow, rather than the usual pierced hide, is the sign the papyrus uses here. The next word is the bolt s over a long cobra ḏ, a flat roll with a tie (Y1) where Budge reads a hand d, the viper f, the coil w over the low hooked sign (U15), water n and ·i (Budge: set'eṭefu-nà, 'wounded [the prey]', his brackets in the English only). It is read sḏfw·n·i by its signs, with the roll as a classifier; no verb of this spelling is known to this edition, and 'wounded' is only Budge's sense. Budge prints sep and sen as two groups; they are joined here as sp sn '(Twice.)' (q re-indexed). The lion hunts with the bow like a king.

sentences.l: I · the-Eye · of-Horus
sentences.i: I am the Eye of Horus.
sentences.n: ink 'I am'. irt ḥr 'the Eye of Horus' is the plain eye with t and its stroke, and the falcon. The dead man is the Eye itself, the healed eye of the god that stands for all that is made whole again.

sentences.l: have-opened-I · the-Eye · of-Horus · [at] · season · this
sentences.i: I have opened the Eye of Horus [at] this season.
sentences.n: sš·n·i is the bolt s, a long rectangle with two oblique strokes inside, coded as the pool š (N37, approximate), a small cross (coded Z9, approximate) over the walking legs as classifiers, water n and ·i: the sḏm·n·f of sš 'open (a door), spread open', 'I have opened' (Budge: seś-nà). irt ḥr 'the Eye of Horus' as before. The mouth r 'at' is printed in Budge's square brackets, restored. tr 'season, time' is t and r, the reed, the stalk tr (M6) and the sun as classifier. pn 'this'. To open the Eye is to restore its sight, which Thoth did for Horus after Seth had damaged it.

sentences.l: have-reached-I · the-riverbanks
sentences.i: I have reached the riverbanks.
sentences.n: pḥ·n·i is the hindquarters of a lion pḥ (coded F22, approximate) over the walking legs, water n and ·i: the sḏm·n·f of pḥ 'reach, arrive at'. wḏbw is a staff topped by a small triangle, the sign wḏ (coded V24, approximate), the foot b, a sinuous sandbank (N20), a small wedge (N21) and plural strokes as classifiers: wḏb 'riverbank, shore', here plural (Budge: uteb, 'the furrows'). The banks are those of the waterways of the world below, or of the river of home.

sentences.l: come · in · peace · Osiris · Ani
sentences.i: Come in peace, O Osiris Ani!
sentences.n: mi 'come!' is the owl m with the arm ꜥ joined to it (the arm not read), the reed i, then water n over the walking legs: the imperative of the verbs of coming, written as if mꜥ, as in Spells 17 and 92 (Budge: māàn, 'let advance'). The water n is not explained and is not read; if it belongs to the word, the sense is doubtful. m ḥtp 'in peace' is the owl and the offering mat with t and p. wsir is the eye, the tall seat and the god; ꜣny has no classifier. The house on earth welcomes its owner back. Spell 132 ends here.

sentences.l: another · spell · of · going-forth · of-a-man · by · day · against · enemies-his · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Another spell for a man's going forth by day against his enemies in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 10 begins (Budge numbers it XLVIII); its title is written in red. ky 'another' is the basket k and two reeds. rꜣ n prt as before. s 'a man' is the bolt, a stroke and the seated man: the subject of the infinitive, 'of a man's going forth'. m hrw 'by day', hrw the sun with its stroke. r 'against'. ḫftyw·f 'his enemies' is ḫ, f, t and the vulture ꜣ, with a kneeling man raising an arm to his head (coded A13, approximate), the classifier of enemies, a thin dashed stroke for the plural, and ·f. m ẖrt-nṯr 'in the necropolis' is written in full: the flag, the block ẖr over a small loop r (coded D21, approximate), and t over the hills (coded N25, approximate).

sentences.l: have-cut(?)-I · the-sky · have-broken-open(?)-I · the-horizon
sentences.i: I have cut through(?) the sky, I have broken open(?) the horizon.
sentences.n: The speech begins with no ḏd in before it. ꜥḏ·n·i is an oval with crossed thread ends, the netting needle ꜥḏ (coded V26, approximate), over the hand d as complement, then a slanting knife (coded T30, approximate) over the low hooked sign (U15) as classifiers, water n and ·i: the sḏm·n·f of a verb ꜥḏ 'cut', taken by its knife (Budge: āṭ-nà, 'I have divided'). pt 'the sky'. Budge's numeral 2 is printed inside the next word, between the jabiru and the vulture: the foot b, the jabiru bꜣ (coded G29, approximate), the vulture ꜣ, the knife (T30, approximate) over U15, water n and ·i: a verb bꜣ written like the word for the ba, here with the knife, taken as 'hack open, break open' (Budge: ba-nà, 'I have passed through'); the sense is doubtful. ꜣḫt 'the horizon' is the sun rising between two hills, t and a house sign. The dead man forces his way out as the sun does at dawn.

sentences.l: have-crossed-I · the-earth · at · strides-his
sentences.i: I have crossed the earth at his stride(?).
sentences.n: šꜣs·n·i is a pool with lotus flowers šꜣ (coded M8, approximate), the vulture ꜣ, the bolt s and the walking legs, water n and ·i: the sḏm·n·f of šꜣs 'travel, cross' (Budge: śas-nà). tꜣ 'the earth' is the strip of land (coded N16, approximate). r 'at'. nmtt·f 'his strides' is the walking legs over t and plural strokes, the legs standing for the whole word, as in Spell 92, and ·f (Budge: nemmat-f). Whose strides are meant is not said: perhaps the sun's, whose course the dead man follows.

sentences.l: have-seized-I · the-spirits · great
sentences.i: I have taken possession of the great spirits.
sentences.n: iṯ·n·i is the tether iṯ standing on walking legs (V15) with t, the low hooked sign (U15), water n and ·i: the sḏm·n·f of iṯi 'take, seize, take possession of'. The form is active, 'I have seized'; Budge's 'I am taken possession of' would need a passive. ꜣḫw 'the spirits' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ and the chick w, a squatting man holding a flail (coded A52, approximate) and a dashed stroke. wrw 'great' is the swallow wr (coded G36, approximate) with r and a stroke, the adjective in the plural.

sentences.l: because · I · indeed · equipped · millions-his · with · magic
sentences.i: for I am indeed one whose millions(?) are equipped with magic.
sentences.n: ḥr-ntt 'because' is the face ḥr with its stroke and ntt, water n and t twice. ink 'I'. Budge's numeral 3 stands before is, the reed and the folded cloth s: the particle is 'indeed', which stresses what precedes. ꜥpr 'equipped' is the bag ꜥpr (Aa20) with r and a flat roll. ḥḥ·f is the kneeling god with raised arms ḥḥ (C11) with a stroke and plural strokes and ·f, 'his millions' (Budge: 'his millions'). m ḥkꜣw 'with magic' is the bar m and the wick ḥ with the raised arms kꜣ over plural strokes and the kneeling man; the w is not written. As it stands, ꜥpr ḥḥ·f is read as an adjective with a noun after it, 'equipped as to his millions', 'one whose millions are equipped'; who 'his' refers to is not said, and the phrase is doubtful.

sentences.l: eat-I · with · mouth-my · chew(?)-I · with · jaw-my
sentences.i: I eat with my mouth, I chew(?) with my jaw.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rꜣ·f; read rꜣ·i. qq·i is the hill-slope q twice, the man with hand to mouth (A2) as the classifier of eating and ·i: qq 'eat' (?) (Budge: qeq-à). m 'with' is the bar m. rꜣ·f is the mouth with its stroke and the viper ·f, over which Budge prints '(sic)'; the speaker is talking of himself, and only 'my mouth' fits. The next word is water n, the vulture ꜣ and a jar-stand g (W11) over an oval with an oblique band (coded Aa2, approximate) as classifier, and ·i (Budge: naḳ-à, 'I chew'): read nꜣg by its signs, a verb not known otherwise to this edition, taken from the parallel with qq as 'chew, crush' (?). m 'with' is the owl. ꜥrt·i 'my jaw' is the arm ꜥ (D36) over r, t over a small curl taken as the jaw sign (coded F19, approximate) and ·i. The dead man eats like the living, with mouth and jaw restored.

sentences.l: I · indeed · the-god · lord · of-the-Duat
sentences.i: I am indeed the god, the lord of the Duat.
sentences.n: ink 'I'. Budge's numeral 4 stands before is 'indeed', the reed and the folded cloth. nṯr 'the god' is the flag with the seated god. nb dwꜣt 'lord of the Duat': the basket nb, and the star, the vulture ꜣ, t and the house sign. The lord of the world below is Osiris, with whom the dead man is one.

sentences.l: (iw) · is-given · to-me · this · to · endure · in · the-Osiris · Ani · this · without(?) · in(?) · appearings-his …
sentences.i: There is given to me this (spell), to endure in this Osiris Ani, without(?) … in(?) his appearings …
sentences.n: iw opens the statement. Budge prints erṭā-n[à] as one group; it is split here into rdi and n·i (q re-indexed). rdi is the mouth r and a flat arm (D36): the passive sḏm of rdi 'give', 'is given'. n·i 'to me' is water n and the seated man, which Budge prints in square brackets, restored. nn 'this' is two rush plants and two water lines: the demonstrative, standing alone as a noun, here taken as the thing given, perhaps the spell itself (Budge: 'that which'). r mn 'to endure': r and mn, the game board (Y5) with n and a flat roll, the infinitive of mn 'be firm, endure' (Budge: men, '[is] everlasting'). m wsir ꜣny pn 'in this Osiris Ani': wsir with the low seat (coded Q2, approximate), and ꜣny, whose kneeling man Budge prints in square brackets, restored. The last words are not clear. The first is the placenta ḫ over a flat bar hooked down at both ends (coded U31, approximate; its value is not clear), t, three water lines, and the arms of negation (D35) as classifier, which belongs to ḫm 'not know, be ignorant of' (Budge: χemt, 'without'); it is read ḫmt by its signs, the three water lines (mw) standing for m, and the t is not explained. m is the bar m. ḫꜥw·f is a hill with rays ḫꜥ (coded N28, approximate) with a flat arm ꜥ (coded D36, approximate), the coil w, a flat roll and ·f: ḫꜥw 'appearings, crowns', from ḫꜥ 'appear in glory' (Budge gives no English for it). Budge's English breaks off here with 'without his' and a row of dots, and Spell 10 ends on the papyrus in mid-thought; what stands is translated, and the sense of the end is doubtful.
